labeling_policy.expected_alpha: Best single MVP-10 alpha if the claim clearly activates one; null when the claim is outside the current taxonomy or should not be force-matched.
labeling_policy.allowed_alpha_ids: Alternative acceptable alpha IDs when a real report sentence blends multiple alphas.
labeling_policy.expected_match_status: matched, ambiguous, or no_match. This intentionally tests no-match and ambiguity behavior, unlike the clean Week 2 gate set.
labeling_policy.expected_direction: Direction of the claim with respect to NVDA or the alpha activation context.

cases.text: NVDA is in a corrective downtrend, trading below short-term moving averages except the 200-day SMA, while RSI and MACD suggest selling pressure may be decelerating.
cases.notes: This is mostly technical trading-state information. The MVP-10 alpha taxonomy does not yet include a technical momentum or support/resistance alpha.

cases.text: The 200-day SMA near $190.63 is acting as long-term structural support, and the long-term trend remains intact as long as NVDA holds above it.
cases.notes: Important investment logic, but outside current MVP-10 alpha taxonomy.

cases.text: NVDA closing below VWMA confirms that volume-weighted activity points to overhead resistance and sellers have dominated higher-volume days.
cases.notes: No corresponding MVP alpha for VWMA/technical supply.

cases.text: The Rubin architecture upgrade forecasts stronger data center revenue ahead and suggests NVIDIA's AI infrastructure spending cycle has a multi-year runway.
cases.notes: Primary is A101 because the causal driver is AI/GPU product-cycle demand. A103 and A301 are acceptable secondary interpretations.

cases.text: NVIDIA and Palantir's sovereign AI partnership expands NVDA's addressable market into defense and government AI infrastructure, a large multi-year and less cyclical vertical.
cases.notes: Primary is infrastructure; it can also support revenue expansion and AI expansion.

cases.text: Etched raising $800 million and disclosing $1 billion of sales contracts confirms the AI chip race is intensifying, but it is a watch item rather than an immediate threat to NVIDIA.
cases.notes: Important real-world risk, but MVP-10 taxonomy lacks a competition/custom-silicon displacement alpha.

cases.text: Etched's chip is reportedly specialized for transformer inference, but the report frames this as niche competition rather than a broad displacement of NVIDIA's ecosystem.
cases.notes: A102 may appear as a surface keyword, but the claim's actual meaning is competitive risk, not inference-demand tailwind.

cases.text: Nvidia, AMD, and Intel led an AI chip stock rally as Wall Street rebounded, showing supportive semiconductor sector momentum.
cases.notes: Could also be A601 if interpreted as investor momentum rather than industry cycle.

cases.text: Retail participation in Magnificent Seven stocks has fallen to a four-year low, which may reduce short-term retail-driven momentum spikes for NVDA.
cases.notes: This is an inverse/weakening narrative-momentum claim; current direction compatibility may struggle because A601 is generally treated as positive.

cases.source_section: News Analyst / NVDY Covered Call ETF Debate
cases.text: Large covered-call ETF activity in NVDY may create near-term ceiling pressure on NVDA as systematic call-selling dampens upside momentum.
cases.notes: This is positioning/flow pressure. MVP taxonomy only partially captures it through narrative momentum.

cases.text: A 78% probability of zero Fed rate cuts in 2026 is a dominant macro risk because higher-for-longer rates compress NVDA's growth multiple.
cases.notes: Primary impact is valuation compression. A001 is secondary because it is the absent/inverted rate-cut cycle.

cases.text: If inflation softens and the Fed pivots, NVDA could re-rate sharply higher through multiple expansion.
cases.notes: Rate cut/pivot is the driver; multiple expansion is the effect.

cases.text: Low U.S. recession probability supports enterprise AI capex budgets and suggests hyperscalers will likely maintain GPU purchasing programs.
cases.notes: This is an inverse recession-risk claim: the risk is low, which is positive for capex. Current rule-based direction may struggle.

cases.text: Dow Jones all-time highs and broad risk-on market conditions support technology and growth exposure.
cases.notes: The text does not say liquidity directly, but risk-on participation is closest to A003 in MVP-10.

cases.text: Rising copper prices are an indirect headwind for hyperscalers building AI infrastructure because copper is a critical data-center input cost.
cases.notes: This is a negative infrastructure bottleneck/cost claim. Keyword rules may miss it because it does not say standard data-center capex phrases cleanly.

cases.text: Weak precious metals suggest reduced safe-haven demand and confidence in risk assets, which is broadly constructive for equities including NVDA.
cases.notes: Closest MVP alpha is A003, though the text is actually a risk-appetite/flow signal rather than liquidity itself.

cases.text: The Rubin architecture uplift, the Palantir sovereign AI partnership, and sector-wide AI chip momentum reinforce NVDA's dominant position in AI infrastructure.
cases.notes: Compound claim. Primary is broad AI expansion; several secondary alphas are defensible.

cases.text: NVDA's pullback to the 200-day SMA with RSI recovering is a buying opportunity rather than a structural breakdown.
cases.notes: Very important trading judgment, but outside current alpha taxonomy.

cases.text: Hyperscalers are competing to build AI capacity, and NVIDIA's Rubin architecture signals that the AI infrastructure spending cycle has years of runway.
cases.notes: Strong A101 signal with A103/A301 downstream effects.

cases.text: NVIDIA's CUDA ecosystem and full-stack GPUs make Etched a niche watch item rather than a broad threat to NVIDIA's AI workload position.
cases.notes: This is moat/competitive positioning, not clean alpha activation. Surface AI keywords may cause false A101.

cases.text: Government AI contracts are large, multi-year, and funded by defense budgets, making NVIDIA's sovereign AI opportunity a defensively positioned growth vertical.
cases.notes: Infrastructure is primary; revenue expansion is secondary.

cases.text: No rate cuts matter less if NVIDIA keeps delivering revenue beats from Blackwell demand, Rubin pre-orders, and government contracts.
cases.notes: Compound rebuttal: revenue growth offsets rate headwind.

cases.text: NVDA is below the 10 EMA, 50 SMA, Bollinger Middle, and VWMA with deeply negative MACD, suggesting a distribution phase and technical breakdown risk.
cases.notes: Technical breakdown risk is not represented by MVP-10 alphas.

cases.text: Rubin revenue is still 12 to 24 months away, and a between-generation air pocket could pressure NVDA if Blackwell demand peaks first.
cases.notes: This is a negative/invalidation form of AI expansion/revenue growth. Keyword matching may misread it as positive.

cases.text: Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta are building custom silicon to reduce their dependency on NVIDIA over time.
cases.notes: This is one of the strongest real bear claims, but MVP-10 lacks a custom-silicon displacement alpha.

cases.text: Higher-for-longer rates compress what investors should pay for NVDA's future earnings and increase the penalty for any earnings disappointment.
cases.notes: Clean multiple compression claim.

cases.text: The Palantir sovereign AI partnership is a press release, not a booked revenue line item, and government procurement can be slow or delayed.
cases.notes: This is negative revenue-conversion risk from an infrastructure catalyst.

cases.text: The bull case wins because the 200-day SMA held on a closing basis, risk-reward is favorable, and fundamental growth drivers such as Rubin, sovereign AI, and CUDA ecosystem expansion remain intact.
cases.notes: The sentence is partly technical/no-match, but the alpha-bearing part is A101/A103/A301.

cases.text: Rate risk is real and zero Fed cuts in 2026 create a valuation ceiling, but it does not justify avoiding NVDA if earnings growth accelerates.
cases.notes: This is an explicit mixed/conflict claim: valuation compression versus revenue expansion.

cases.text: Hyperscaler custom silicon is the strongest structural bear argument, but it is a four-to-six-year story against a rapidly expanding AI compute market.
cases.notes: Real structural conflict not cleanly represented in MVP-10. It should not be forced into A101 just because the AI market is mentioned.
